claims.boundary: Average rise on 18 AI-financing news days after controls; the response faded within two trading days.

source.title: BIS Bulletin No 140: Building AI on credit: structures and spillovers

claims.quote: On AI-financing-related news days in 2026, spillovers to US Treasury and investment-grade bond markets were small and short-lived, but sustained issuance at the current pace could change this._ ... These AI investments are increasingly built on credit. Gross bond issuance this year by the five largest hyperscalers reached $222 billion by September 2026 (Graph 1.B). Most of this debt was issued at long maturities, amounting to more than 10% of long-term US Treasury issuance this year. In addition, debt is raised through off-balance sheet vehicles. ² According to market sources, $75 to $100 billion of bonds and asset-backed securities linked to these vehicles have been placed so far this year. And the commitments behind these structures are also large. Moody’s Ratings (2026), for example, puts the largest hyperscalers’ data centre lease commitments at $1.2 trillion by mid-2026, of which around $820 billion relate to leases that have not yet started. ... 2 Aldasoro et al (2026) document the shift in AI financing from cash flows to debt and the growing role of private credit as investors. Eren et al (2026) document the increased role of off-balance sheet structures through which the borrowing is raised. ... Off-balance sheet vehicles can draw institutional capital into the build-out by combining asset backing with lease commitments, guarantees and vendor backstops. But the structures obscure the final allocation of risks, and ultimate exposures are concentrated in a few large firms – more than what their balance sheets suggest. The second question involves broader spillovers from the borrowing. Much of the new debt is long- dated and placed with non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) that also hold long-dated government and investment-grade corporate bonds. A growing supply could therefore affect the compensation these investors require for bearing duration risk, with consequences for benchmark yields and borrowing costs beyond the AI sector. This Bulletin finds that so far, such spillovers have been limited. On AI-financing- related news days in 2026, movements in Treasury term premia and investment-grade corporate spreads were small and short-lived. But sustained issuance at the current pace could make them larger and more persistent.
